passes.label: security:d-compile
passes.checked:
Commit 7b36d27 exists. Frozen copy: /home/user/taskdeck/target/work/check-security-d-compile. Scratch tests: crates/taskdeck-core/tests/zz_security.rs, and a block at the end of crates/taskdeck-core/tests/compile.rs whose tests start with `zz_`. Both are in the copy, and W was not touched.

parse_intent, tried by hand:
- The 84,096-byte check runs before any parsing.
- Refused with intent_json: nesting 5000 deep (serde's recursion limit, no stack overflow); a duplicate known field; a duplicate `op`, including one written with escapes; a float or exponent for an integer; -0; 1e400; a lone surrogate; an integer `op`; a non-string wire time.
- u64::MAX ids are accepted and come back as item_gone.
- Wire times are read as chrono reads them: lowercase t/z, a space separator, single-digit fields and `+12345` years give Exact or Naive. A naive leap second becomes Naive; an exact one is refused.
- Unknown fields are ignored, duplicated or not.
- Memory used while the unknown fields are buffered stays around 10 to 20 times the input, so about 1 MB at most.

compile:
- Every row against §13.4's step order.
- A property test of 4000 cases: page-style JSON with edge values (ids 2^53−1, 2^53, u64::MAX; i32::MIN/MAX and u32::MAX for start and minutes; days 1970-01-01, 9999-12-31, +10000; naive and exact edge times; names and URLs with NUL, U+0085, U+00A0, U+3000, U+FEFF, U+200B, U+10FFFF and 200-scalar names; webcal/https/random URLs; set_home edge values; any [u8;4] colors) across random boards, table zones and overlays. Every command returned parses after encoding and is accepted by apply on the view, except set_notes with an explicit base (finding 2).
- Minter: at 2^40−1 and at u64::MAX it answers cap_items or cap_blocks and does not move on error, including a create of a task whose block mint fails.
- checked_url: lengths 9 and 2000, webcal, trim.
- name_from_url: the result is never empty.
- Views at their caps: a reflow with 50 tasks × 1000 blocks plus 9,950 daily routines takes 181 ms in release and 1.36 s in debug. A restore of a 1000-block row against 49,000 live blocks takes 67 ms in release. Neither is a finding.

Not covered:
- compile against a view near the 59 MiB size cap, where every intent also costs canonical_len, a board clone and an apply.
- Very large overlays in reflow.
- ChronoZone with real DST rules (only FixedZone and TableZone).
- read::reflow_inputs beyond the at-caps run.

serious.title: parse_intent accepts a JSON array as an intent: `["forget",5]` parses as Forget{id:5}, `["rename",3,"n"]` as Rename, `["quick_add","x",null]` as QuickAdd
serious.clause: core.md §12.2 step 2 ("it is a JSON object with a string field `op`", else core/intent_json); CORE-INT-001 ("MUST return core/intent_json with status 400 for every other input")

serious.title: compile emits set_notes with the intent's raw u64 `base`; at 2^53 or above the command encodes to empty bytes, which parse_command refuses as core/not_json
serious.clause: CORE-COMP-008 (every returned command MUST pass parse_command after canonical encoding); §9.20 `base` is u53; §4.2 rule 5

unreproduced: At a view near the 59 MiB size cap, each compile call runs canonical_len, a full board clone and an apply on the copy (apply::refused_for_size). If the page fills the board to that size, every later intent probably costs hundreds of ms. Not measured.

planner::reflow is O(flowables × anchors) with no cap on the overlay's anchors. Reflow against a large overlay is probably slow, but the overlay comes from ICS feeds, not from the intent. Not measured.

fixed: parse_intent accepted a JSON array as an intent. I added the test an_array_is_not_an_intent to crates/taskdeck-core/tests/compile.rs. It covers the three inputs from the report plus one with leading whitespace, and it failed at 7b36d27. The fix is in crates/taskdeck-core/src/intent.rs, parse_intent, at §12.2 step 2. After leading JSON whitespace, text that starts with '[' is refused before the serde derive reads it. The error is core/intent_json, status 400, with the message "invalid type: sequence, expected internally tagged enum Command". This stops the internally tagged visitor's visit_seq from reading the array. Any other non-object is still refused by the derive with its own message. I checked the text's first byte instead of parsing through a serde_json::Value, so the derive's error messages, including the 'not a time' message the vectors compare, stay as they were.

compile copied an unchecked u64 set_notes base into the command, so a base of 2^53 or more encoded to empty bytes. I added the test set_notes_base_beyond_u53_is_not_emitted to tests/compile.rs. It runs with base 2^53 and with u64::MAX, and it failed at 7b36d27 with Err(core/not_json). The fix is in crates/taskdeck-core/src/compile.rs, in the Intent::SetNotes arm. After resolving the default, compile refuses any base above MAX_U53 (2^53-1, a new private const) with core/notes_stale, status 400, and a new message. Such a base can never equal view.notes_rev, which is a u53, so apply on view would refuse it with that same code. Every SetNotes command compile returns now encodes and parses again (CORE-COMP-008). I added core/notes_stale to compile's fail() table and marked it with a SPEC-QUESTION.
Gate: cargo test, clippy --all-targets -D warnings, ci.sh and gate.sh --only purity-clippy-toml core all ran in one && chain, which exited 0.
for_lead: core.md §13.4 set_notes row and §16: there is no compile refusal for an intent base above 2^53-1, but §12.3 types the intent field as u64. Reading A: refuse it in parse_intent as core/intent_json, with the intent field typed u53. Reading B: refuse it in compile with apply's code, core/notes_stale. I took B, with status 400 and a new message, and marked it with a SPEC-QUESTION in compile.rs (fail table and SetNotes arm). The spec should say which one it wants and list core/notes_stale under compile in §16 if B stands.

Still open from before, at the existing SPEC-QUESTION in the compile.rs SetNotes arm: an intent base below 2^53 that differs from view.notes_rev is emitted as given, so apply on view refuses it core/notes_stale, which goes against CORE-COMP-008. Also, a view.notes_rev of 2^53-1 has no compile code (apply refuses it core/cap). The spec needs a ruling on both: either refuse in compile or exempt set_notes from CORE-COMP-008's 'accepted by apply' clause.
